show_hn.title: Show HN: A language model that lives in a boot sector
show_hn.story_text: All the ideas came from the boot sector demo scene where people had been writing chess and BASIC games in 512 bytes, even a C compiler. I wondered what one can do using a neural network instead of a program and generating boot logs for non-existent hardware was something fun to try. Entire inference engine is 510 bytes of MBR, weights, vocab, and strings reside in the sectors following MBR. Small char-level neural network was trained on dmesg generated by machine, so machine produces Linux boot messages infinitely. train.py performs precisely the same integer arithmetic operations as the asm code does and thus produces an output identical character-by-character to the one produced by QEMU. show_hn.title: Show HN: CheckOwners to find your repo's hidden single points of failure
show_hn.story_text:
Hey HN Community! I created checkOwners to solve a problem by many engineering teams: who knows your codebase, and what will happen when they go away? This is an open-source, local-first tool which performs analysis based on Git history in order to find hidden knowledge risk in repositories. It is able to recognize true experts, recognize out-of-date ownership definitions, find knowledge bottlenecks, propose review candidates, and model what would happen when contributors go away. All the magic happens on your own local system without uploading source code or an LLM. It also works within GitHub Actions. Try it:
```
pip install checkowners
checkowners audit
checkowners risk
``` Would appreciate any feedback from maintainers and platform engineers regarding the accuracy of Git history reflec
